notes.text: In chs. 23–27 David continues to prepare for Solomon’s rule by providing religious, military, and political leadership.

A legitimate census of the Levites, as in Num. 4:1–3 (see 1 Chron. 21:1–17 and notes on 1 Chronicles 21:1–17). The age of beginning service (thirty . . . and upward) was later lowered to 20 (23:24, 27). 38,000. The Hebrew word here for “thousand” may denote “groups” or “units” of unknown size.
David organizes the Levites according to their traditional clans: the Gershonites (vv. 7–11), the Kohathites (vv. 12–20), and the Merarites (vv. 21–23).
David appears as the successor to Moses (see Numbers 4) as he defines the Levites’ duties in relation to the temple.
